title: The nine reminders
hookLine: Marcus lists nine things to recall when offended: we're made for each other, they act from beliefs, we err too (Meditations 11.18)

cards: Someone offends you, and the old script starts running: how dare they, who do they think they are, wait till I tell everyone. Marcus wrote a different script.
It's a long entry, numbered first, second, third, like a pilot's checklist before takeoff. He wrote it to read when someone offended him, a list to run before the reply goes out.

teach.h: ONE TO THREE: KIN, BELIEFS, IGNORANCE.
teach.b: First, about them. One: we're made for one another. Two: think what these people are like at the table, in bed, and what beliefs are driving them.
Three: if they're right, don't complain; if they're wrong, it's unwillingly, out of ignorance. No soul, Marcus says, is willingly cut off from the truth. Second, about you.

teach.h: FOUR TO SIX: ME TOO, UNSURE, BRIEF.
teach.b: Four: you do plenty of wrong yourself, and even when you don't, you have the tendency, held back only by fear or concern for your reputation.

Five: you don't even know for certain that they're doing wrong; many things are done for reasons you can't see. Six: when you're furious, remember that life is a moment, and soon we'll all be laid out.
Third, about the anger. Seven: it isn't their acts that disturb us; those live in them. It's our own judgments.

teach.h: SEVEN AND EIGHT: MY JUDGMENT, MY ANGER.
teach.b: Take away the judgment that it's terrible, and the anger goes with it. Eight: our anger and grief hurt us more than the things that caused them. Fourth, the last.
Nine: kindness is invincible, if it's real, not a fake smile or an act.

What can the most violent person do if you stay kind, and at the very moment they try to harm you, gently say: no, my child, we were made for something else; you won't harm me, you're harming yourself, my child.
Then Marcus adds a tenth, as a gift, he says, from the leader of the Muses: to expect bad people not to do wrong is madness.

how: Some readers of the Meditations copy out the nine reminders and reread them when someone has offended them, often before replying.

o: Marcus's gentle words to someone trying to harm him
a phrase Marcus used to scold a lazy servant
what Marcus called his son when giving him advice

games.q: the nine reminders — tap the pairs.
p: it's my judgment that disturbs me

s: Marcus says people who do wrong do it willingly
reminder three: if they're wrong, it's unwillingly, out of ignorance.
he adds a tenth reminder, as a gift from the leader of the Muses
expecting bad people not to do wrong, he says, is madness.

games.q: someone tries to harm you, right now, in front of you. you're Marcus with reminder nine. what do you say?
o: gently: no, my child, we were made for something else; you're harming yourself.
games.why: kindness is invincible if it's genuine, he writes, and gives himself those very words for the moment the other tries to harm him.

practice: Bring to mind one person who offended you recently, and run the nine slowly: we're made for each other; they act from their beliefs; if they're wrong, it's unwilling; I've done the same; I can't be sure; life is short; it's my judgment that hurts; my anger hurts more; kindness can't be beaten.
Let each one land for a breath, and notice which one loosens the knot.

wordCard.voice: My child. Marcus's gentle answer to real harm: no, my child, we were made for something else; you're only harming yourself. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: unconquerable, invincible. Marcus's word for genuine kindness in reminder nine.

carryVoice: Your line: nine reminders. Even three of them can slow the reply. See you tomorrow.
